methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $23M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Podium Automation is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $23M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private firms and one public company (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector, including Series B-stage peers Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity, alongside earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement to the $23M total raised proxy, yielding $46M. Peer-median benchmarking across four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $1.7B implied valuation, with the peer range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The substantial dispersion reflects both stage heterogeneity within the peer set and variance in market timing and capital efficiency across firms.

The triangulated range spans $39M (floor) to $2.0B (ceiling), with a median of $873M. The wide spread reflects structural uncertainty: stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge by over 30x, driven primarily by peer-set heterogeneity and the application of different benchmarking anchors. Key uncertainties include Podium's relative maturity versus the peer cohort, revenue scale and margin trajectory, and capital efficiency relative to Series B-stage exits. Further diligence on unit economics and market adoption would materially narrow this range.
